source.title: OPEN QUESTIONS FOR OPERATORS RELATED TO RECTANGULAR CATALAN COMBINATORICS

accepted.question_text: For a partition μ of d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let Θ_{a,b}: Λ → E be the elliptic-Hall-algebra monomorphism used in the paper, and let s^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(s_μ)(1). Writing ι(μ) = Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ(μ)} χ(μ_i - i), is the renormalized symmetric function (-qt)^(-ι(μ)) s^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,t) always Schur-positive, meaning that its Schur expansion has coefficients in N[q,t]? If yes, can this positivity be explained by exhibiting a bigraded S_n-subrepresentation of the generalized diagonal harmonics module whose bigraded Frobenius characteristic is this expression?
accepted.context_brief: Schur positivity of renormalized Schur-seed operators

evidence.quote: Because of ties with representation theory, we are interested in functions fd such that the application of the operators Θa,b(fd) to the constant symmetric function 1 gives Schur-positive symmetric function, for any coprime a, b ≥ 1. When this is so, we say that fd gives rise to Schur-positive operators, and denote by f(a,b)d (x; q, t) the symmetric function Θa,b(fd)(1).
the renormalized Schur functions (−qt)−ι(µ) sµ(x) where, for an integer partition µ of d, we set ι(µ) := Σℓ(µ)i=1 χ(µ(i) − i);

Question.1. Can we prove that 0 ⪯s (−qt)−ι(µ) s(a,b)µ (x, q, t), for all partition µ of d, and all coprime a, b ≥ 1? Can we explain this in terms of bigraded subrepresentations of the Sn-module of generalized diagonal harmonics?

accepted.question_text: For a partition μ of d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let m^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(m_μ)(1). Is the renormalized symmetric function (-1)^(d-ℓ(μ)) m^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,t) always Schur-positive, i.e. does it always expand in the Schur basis with coefficients in N[q,t]? Preferably, can one realize these expressions as bigraded Frobenius characteristics of suitable bigraded S_n-modules?

evidence.quote: or more generally, the monomial symmetric functions (−1)n−ℓ(µ) mµ(x).
Question.2. Can we prove that 0 ⪯s (−1)d−ℓ(µ) m(a,b)µ (x; q, t), for all partition µ of d, and all coprime a, b ≥ 1?
Preferably, this would be explained by introducing adequate bigraded Sn-modules whose bigraded Forbenius characteristic would correspond to these Schur positive expressions.

accepted.question_text: Let s_(j|k)(x) denote the hook-indexed Schur function for the hook partition with one part of size j+1 and k parts equal to 1, and write s^{(a,b)}_λ(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(s_λ)(1). Also, when (m,n) = (ad,bd) with d = gcd(m,n), write e_{m,n}(x;q,t) for e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) and h_{m,n}(x;q,t) for h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t), and let β = α(m,n) - d + 1 be the number of lattice points between the diagonal-avoiding (m,n)-staircase path and the (m-1,n)-staircase path. For all coprime a,b ≥ 1, all j,k, and all m,n ≥ 1, can one prove both Schur-positivity inequalities q(-1)^j s^{(a,b)}_(j+1|k-1)(x;q,t) ⪯_s (-1)^(j-1) s^{(a,b)}_(j|k)(x;q,t) and q^β e_{m-1,n}(x;q,t) ⪯_s (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}(x;q,t)?

evidence.quote: where s(j | k)(x) stands for the hook indexed Schur symmetric functions, where the hook has one part of size j + 1, and k parts of 1.

it is convenient to denote by fm,n(x; q, t) the symmetric function f(a,b)d (x; q, t), when (m, n) = (ad, bd) and d = gcd(m, n). Then, let us write fm,n(x; q, t) ⪯s gm,n(x; q, t), if and only if the difference gm,n(x; q, t) − fm,n(x; q, t) is Schur-positive.

qβ em−1,n(x; q, t) ⪯s (−qt)1−dhm,n(x; q, t), with β = α(m, n) − d + 1, for d = gcd(m, n). In other words, this is the number of points that lie between the diagonal avoiding (m, n)-staircase path, and the (m − 1, n)-staircase path.
Question. 3. Can we prove that, for all coprime a, b ≥ 1, all j and k, and all m, n ≥ 1, inequalities (3.4) and (3.5) hold?

accepted.question_text: When (m,n) = (ad,bd) with d = gcd(m,n), write e_{m,n}(x;q,t) := e^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) and h_{m,n}(x;q,t) := h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t). Let α′ = α′(m,n) be the number of integer points between the (m,n-1)-staircase path and the minimal (m,n)-staircase, and let β′ be the analogous exponent appearing in the transpose version of the complete-homogeneous inequality. For every pair m,n ≥ 1, can one prove the Schur-positivity inequalities q^{α′} e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t) ⪯_s e_{m,n}(x;q,t) and q^{β′} e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t) ⪯_s (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}(x;q,t), preferably by explaining them as inclusions of bigraded representations?
accepted.context_brief: Transpose Schur inclusions for elementary and complete seeds

evidence.quote: we have observed that, similarly to (3.2), we have qα′ em,n−1(x; q, t) ⪯s em,n(x; q, t). In this case, much as before, α′ = α′(m, n) is the number of integer points between the (m, n − 1)-staircase path and the minimal (m, n)-staircase.
Once again, there seems to be a transpose version of this qβ′ em,n−1(x; q, t) ⪯s (−qt)1−d hm,n(x; q, t), with β′ defined suitably.
Question.4. Can we prove that, for all pair m, n ≥ 1, inequalities (3.3) and (3.6) hold? Preferably, these “facts” would be explained in terms of inclusion of bigraded representations.

accepted.question_text: Let f_d be any seed whose associated operators are Schur-positive, and write f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(f_d)(1). Let the linear operator overline{·} on Schur functions be defined by overline{s_μ} = s_{ ar μ}, where  ar μ is obtained by removing the first column of μ, and extend this operator linearly so expressions of different total degree can be compared. For coprime integers b ≥ a ≥ 1, is it always true that f^{(b,a)}_d(x;q,t) ⪯_s f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,t) after this comparison, for every seed f_d that gives rise to Schur-positive expressions?

evidence.quote: For a partition µ, let us denote by µ̄ the partition obtained by removing the first column of µ. Then, we set sµ(x) := sµ̄(x), and extend linearly to all symmetric functions.
Question.5. Can we prove that f(b,a)d (x; q, t) ⪯s f(a,b)d (x; q, t), for all coprime b ≥ a ≥ 1, and any seed fd that gives rise to Schur positive expressions?

We underline that the functions f(b,a)d (x; q, t) and f(a,b)d (x; q, t) are of different degrees; equal to ad in the first case, and bd in the second. Hence they can only be compared after applying the (−) operator, which results in a symmetric function having components of various degrees.

accepted.question_text: For any seed f_d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let Θ_{a,b}(f_d) be the corresponding operator and let f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1) denote its value on 1 after specializing t = 1. Does the specialized operator Θ_{a,b}(f_d)|_{t=1} act on every symmetric function g(x) simply as multiplication by f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1)? Equivalently, can one prove the multiplicativity relation (f_d g_k)^{(a,b)}(x;q,1) = f^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1) g^{(a,b)}_k(x;q,1) for all seeds and all coprime a,b ≥ 1?
accepted.context_brief: Multiplicativity of specialized operators at t = 1

evidence.quote: Indeed, one observes experimentally that Θa,b(fd)(g(x))|t=1 = f(a,b)d (x; q, 1) · g(x).
Implicit in statement (4.1) is the “multiplicativity” (fd gk)(a,b)(x; q, 1) = f(a,b)d (x; q, 1) g(a,b)k (x; q, 1). Thus all of this would follow from the following:
Question. 6. Can we prove that the operator Θa,b(fd)|t=1 operates by multiplication by f(a,b)d (x; q, 1), for all seed fd and all coprime a, b ≥ 1?

accepted.question_text: For integers j,k with j + k = d - 1 and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1+r) and s^{(a,b)}_(j|k)(x;q,1+r) be the specialized symmetric functions obtained from the corresponding seeds by the operators Θ_{a,b}. Using the order ≤_e for e-positivity, meaning that the difference has nonnegative coefficients in the elementary symmetric basis, can one prove both 0 ≤_e (-1)^(1-k) h^{(a,b)}_d(x;q,1+r) and q(-1)^j s^{(a,b)}_(j+1|k-1)(x;q,1+r) ≤_e (-1)^(j-1) s^{(a,b)}_(j|k)(x;q,1+r) for all such j,k,a,b?
accepted.context_brief: e-positivity at t = 1 + r for complete and hook seeds

evidence.quote: If f is e-positive, we write 0 ≤e f. This is clearly stronger than Schur-positivity, since it is classical that each eµ is itself Schur-positive.
Question.7. Can we prove that 0 ≤e (−1)1−kh(a,b)d (x; q, 1 + r), and q (−1)j s(a,b)(j+1 | k−1)(x; q, 1 + r) ≤e (−1)j−1 s(a,b)(j | k)(x; q, 1 + r), for all j + k = d − 1, and all coprime a, b ≥ 1?

accepted.question_text: For a partition μ of d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1, let m^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,1+r) := Θ_{a,b}(m_μ)(1) specialized at t = 1 + r. Is the renormalized symmetric function (-1)^(d-ℓ(μ)) m^{(a,b)}_μ(x;q,1+r) always e-positive, meaning that its expansion in the elementary symmetric basis has coefficients in N[q,r]? If it is, can this e-positivity be explained by a direct combinatorial enumeration analogous to the Dyck-path formula discussed earlier in the paper?
accepted.context_brief: e-positivity of monomial-seed operators at t = 1 + r

evidence.quote: Question.8. Can we prove that, for any partition µ of d, and any coprime a, b ≥ 1, that 0 ≤e (−1)d−ℓ(µ) m(a,b)µ (x; q, 1 + r), in other words, that the symmetric functions are e-positive?
Furthermore, can we explain this e-positivity in terms of a combinatorial enumeration in the style of (4.4)?

accepted.question_text: For integers m,n ≥ 1, let e_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) and h_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) denote the t = 1 + r specializations of the symmetric functions attached to the elementary and complete homogeneous seeds, with d = gcd(m,n), α the exponent from the inclusion q^α e_{m-1,n} into e_{m,n}, and β = α(m,n) - d + 1 the exponent from the inclusion into (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}. In the e-positivity order ≤_e, can one prove q^α e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) ≤_e e_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) and q^β e_{m-1,n}(x;q,1+r) ≤_e (-qt)^(1-d) h_{m,n}(x;q,1+r) for all m,n ≥ 1, and give a combinatorial explanation of these inequalities?
accepted.context_brief: e-positive refinements of Schur inclusions at t = 1 + r

evidence.quote: Question.9. Can we prove that qα em−1,n(x; q, 1 + r) ≤e em,n(x; q, 1 + r), and qβ em−1,n(x; q, 1 + r) ≤e (−qt)1−dhm,n(x; q, 1 + r). for all m, n ≥ 1, and explain this combinatorially?
qβ em−1,n(x; q, t) ⪯s (−qt)1−dhm,n(x; q, t), with β = α(m, n) − d + 1, for d = gcd(m, n).
